title: Drone strike by Sudan paramilitary kills 41 near Ethiopian border, rights group says
summary:
A drone attack by Sudan's paramilitary forces has killed 41 people in the country's Blue Nile region bordering Ethiopia, a rights group has said.
The strike by the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) targeted a camp for displaced people in the state's Abu Shandi area on Friday, Emergency Lawyers said.
The UN Office for the Co-ordination of Humanitarian Affairs (Ocha) said it was "appalled by horrifying reports".
The Sudanese army and paramilitary forces including the RSF have been locked in a power struggle since 2023, a conflict that has killed hundreds of thousands and displaced more than 14 million from their homes.
It has also created one of the worst humanitarian crises in the world, with millions of people needing medical help.

title: US ICE releases Kashmiri filmmaker Arfat Sheikh from custody
summary:
Award-winning filmmaker, who was detained last month, released on bond with next hearing set for October 27, campaign says.
The Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agency in the United States has released Kashmiri filmmaker Arfat Sheikh from custody after he was detained on September 24.
However, ICE’s deportation case against Sheikh continues with the next hearing set for October 27, the campaign said.
Sheikh’s first feature film, Saffron Kingdom, garnered multiple honours, notably best feature film at the Chicago Filmmakers Awards, Los Angeles Film and Documentary Awards, Melbourne Independent Film Festival, Wake Forest Film Festival and Anatolian International Film Awards.

title: Asylum seekers buying sick notes online to dodge Home Office interviews
summary:
Asylum seekers are buying sick notes online to dodge Home Office interviews about their claim, the Mail can reveal.
The tactic is allegedly being used so claimants can delay asylum interviews for up to six months, buying them time to build their claim and continue working in the UK.
A Home Office source told the Mail that these sick notes are being used as 'time-buying devices' by claimants.
The Home Office declined to answer a Freedom of Information request asking how many asylum interviews had been postponed after claimants had submitted sick notes.
Asylum seekers are buying sick notes such as this online from Home2Lab, allegedly to dodge Home Office interviews.

title: US suspends Microsoft and seven other firms from green card programme
summary:
The US government has suspended Microsoft and seven other technology companies from a federal programme that lets employers sponsor foreign workers for green cards.
Vice President JD Vance made the call at a White House press conference.
Vice President JD Vance announced the decision at the White House on Thursday and accused the companies of fraud.
This means H-1B workers at these companies can keep their jobs, but their employers cannot begin a green card process for them through PERM.
“Our message to Microsoft is: You’re a great American company, but you’ve got to hire great American workers,” Vance said.
